target.title: The Farmer's Fleet
target.premise: You are visiting a cozy countryside petting farm to adopt a fluffy companion.
target.phrase: Can I have that sheep, please?
target.phrase_ipa: k ə n aɪ h æ v ð æ t ʃ iː p p l iː z

narrative.scene: Barnaby is waiting by the farm gate. His small woolly companion trots over beside him.
narrative.prompt: Barnaby has a friend who needs a home too. Which one would you like me to bring over?
narrative.intended_dialogue: Another sheep! I will put two little name tags on the meadow gate.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Another ship? The delivery driver is looking for a harbour on my farm map!

narrative.scene: A delivery captain has brought a vessel to the farm. Giles has opened a very small returns desk.
narrative.prompt: The captain can take that delivery back. Tell me what you wanted to adopt instead.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A sheep! The captain takes his delivery away while I fetch a woolly companion.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A ship again? The captain has started measuring the duck pond!

narrative.scene: Two woolly companions are ready for their new home. A tiny third animal peeks through the fence.
narrative.prompt: This little one would rather travel with the others. Ask me to bring it to the gate.
narrative.intended_dialogue: The third sheep joins its friends. That is a very cosy adoption day!
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A third ship order? I have sent the driver a photograph of our tiny farm gate.

narrative.scene: Barnaby is safe by the gate, but a captain is waiting beside the second delivery form.
narrative.prompt: Let us fix the second form before the lorry arrives. Ask again for the companion you want.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Sheep is on the corrected form. Barnaby gets a friend instead of a delivery dock.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Ship is back on the form. Barnaby has become the farm shipping inspector!

narrative.scene: The captain has collected the mistaken delivery. Giles returns with a fluffy animal in his arms.
narrative.prompt: Before I write the adoption certificate, confirm what you are taking home.
narrative.intended_dialogue: One sheep, confirmed! The certificate comes with a little bag of meadow hay.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: One ship, confirmed? I had better ask the captain to turn round again!

narrative.scene: The captain has measured the duck pond and shaken his head. Giles holds up the adoption form.
narrative.prompt: Our pond cannot become a harbour. Try the adoption request one last time.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A sheep at last! The ducks can keep their pond and your new pet can keep its meadow.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A ship it is, then. The ducks have appointed themselves the harbour committee!

target.title: The Exam Frying Trap
target.premise: You sit down at the university examination hall, but your writing instrument is missing.
target.phrase: Excuse me, could you lend me a pen?
target.phrase_ipa: ɪ k s k j uː z m iː k ʊ d j uː l e n d m iː ə p e n

narrative.scene: Your ballpoint is ready. The professor notices that the next exam desk has no spare writing tool.
narrative.prompt: Your neighbour needs to start the diagram too. Ask me for another writing tool.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Here is a spare pen. Both exam desks are ready for their first answers.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pan for your neighbour? I will need a much larger pencil case!

narrative.scene: A heavy skillet sits beside your blank exam paper. The professor has reopened the supply cupboard.
narrative.prompt: That belongs in the canteen. Tell me what you need to write your answer.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen, of course! The skillet goes back to the canteen and your answer can begin.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Another pan? The canteen thinks our exam has become a cookery lesson.

narrative.scene: Both students can write. The professor approaches with a form for the last page of the exam.
narrative.prompt: The spare ink has run out just as you reach the final page. Ask for a replacement.
narrative.intended_dialogue: One fresh pen for the final answer. You can finish before the bell.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: One pan for the final answer? The invigilator is checking whether the question asks for an omelette.

narrative.scene: You can write, but your neighbour has received a skillet. The professor wheels over the supply trolley.
narrative.prompt: Let us replace your neighbour's unusual equipment. Make the request again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen replaces the skillet. Your neighbour finally gets to draw the diagram.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pan stays on the desk. Your neighbour is using it as an enormous paperweight.

narrative.scene: The skillet has returned to the canteen. Your first answer is written and the professor brings a sign-in sheet.
narrative.prompt: The sign-in desk needs its writing tool back. Ask for one to finish your name.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Here is a pen for the sign-in sheet. The professor can finally count a full room of students.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pan for the sign-in sheet? Nobody has invented ink-proof frying pans yet.

narrative.scene: Two skillets have reached the exam hall. The professor places them on the canteen returns trolley.
narrative.prompt: We will settle this at the stationery cupboard. Ask for the tool that belongs with an exam paper.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen comes straight from the stationery shelf. The exam can finally begin.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pan comes straight from the canteen. The professor has written a very unusual incident report.

target.title: The Valentine Shelter
target.premise: You are writing a romantic love poem to your sweetheart on Valentine's Day.
target.phrase: You hold the key to my heart.
target.phrase_ipa: j uː h əʊ l d ð ə k iː t ə m aɪ h ɑː t

narrative.scene: The gold pendant bears your romantic message. The florist sets a matching gift card beside it.
narrative.prompt: The card can carry the same message. Dictate it once more for the calligrapher.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Your heart appears in flowing script on the card. It matches the pendant beautifully.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Your hut appears on the card. The calligrapher has added a little door and a chimney.

narrative.scene: The pendant has been engraved with a woodland shelter. The florist brings a fresh gold blank.
narrative.prompt: We can remake it before gift wrapping. Dictate the romantic message again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Your heart is now on the new pendant. The woodland design goes in our sample drawer.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Your hut is on the new pendant too. The sample drawer is becoming a tiny village.

narrative.scene: The pendant and card match. The florist offers a ribbon tag for the final wrapped gift.
narrative.prompt: Let us give the ribbon tag the same message. Dictate it for the final time.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Your heart completes the ribbon tag. The gift is ready for a romantic evening.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Your hut completes the tag. Your sweetheart may wonder whether the gift comes with a garden.

narrative.scene: The pendant is romantic, but the matching card shows a small woodland shelter.
narrative.prompt: The card artist has a clean sheet ready. Dictate the message that belongs beside the pendant.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Your heart replaces the shelter drawing. The card and pendant finally tell the same story.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Your hut stays on the card. We have given it a very romantic flower box.

narrative.scene: The replacement pendant has the romantic message. The florist prepares the gift box lid.
narrative.prompt: Confirm the wording before I add it to the lid.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Your heart is written on the lid. The replacement gift is ready to wrap.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Your hut is written on the lid. The florist wonders whether a tiny house key belongs inside.

narrative.scene: Two shelter-shaped engravings sit in the sample drawer. The florist brings one last plain pendant.
narrative.prompt: We have a whole village of samples now. Dictate the message for this final plain pendant.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Your heart makes a lovely final engraving. The little village can stay in the sample drawer.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Your hut becomes the final engraving. The florist wraps it in paper decorated with tiny roofs.

target.title: The Royal Banquet
target.premise: The Emperor's grand feast is ending and the waiter offers you a fifth slice of roast beef.
target.phrase: No thank you, I am completely full.
target.phrase_ipa: n əʊ θ æ ŋ k j uː aɪ æ m k ə m p l iː t l i f ʊ l

narrative.scene: The butler removes the roast platter. A dessert trolley arrives with a very large pudding.
narrative.prompt: Perhaps a generous helping of pudding? Tell me whether you have room.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Still full! I will leave the pudding on the trolley and bring a small cup of tea.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A fool at the pudding trolley? The jester is checking whether that is his cue.

narrative.scene: The court jester has heard the remark and stepped forward. The butler returns with the covered dish.
narrative.prompt: Let us clear up the misunderstanding. Tell me politely why you do not want another helping.
narrative.intended_dialogue: You are full! I understand now. The jester bows and I take the serving dish away.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A fool again? The jester has begun an unexpected after-dinner performance.

narrative.scene: The roast and pudding have been declined. A servant offers a towering plate of biscuits with your tea.
narrative.prompt: Shall we add a few biscuits? Give me your reply once more.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Completely full, understood. Tea alone will finish the evening nicely.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Completely fool? The jester balances a biscuit on his hat and takes another bow.

narrative.scene: The roast is gone, but the dessert trolley has become the jester's stage. The butler moves it aside.
narrative.prompt: Before the pudding becomes part of the act, repeat your reply to my offer.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Full, of course. The trolley returns to the kitchen and the jester returns to his seat.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Fool once more? The jester has invited the pudding trolley to take a bow.

narrative.scene: The jester has accepted the explanation. The butler notices another waiter approaching with pastries.
narrative.prompt: I will pass your reply to the pastry waiter. Please say it again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Full is the message I will pass on. The pastries travel to the next table.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Fool is the message? The pastry waiter asks whether the jester ordered the tray.

narrative.scene: The unexpected performance has grown into a juggling act. The butler quietly returns to your place.
narrative.prompt: The entertainment can wait. Give me your reply about the food one last time.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Full at last! The feast ends with a bow, a cleared table and a peaceful cup of tea.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Fool it is! The jester announces an encore while the butler guards the dessert trolley.

target.title: The Cooking Shop Mix-up
target.premise: You are buying a saucepan for a cooking class at a little kitchen shop.
target.phrase: Can I have a pot, please?
target.phrase_ipa: k ə n aɪ h æ v ə p ɒ t p l iː z

narrative.scene: A sturdy saucepan is on the kitchen-shop counter. The shopkeeper shows you a smaller one for tomorrow's lunch.
narrative.prompt: You may need a second cooking vessel for the smaller batch. Ask me for what you want.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A smaller pot joins the order. Both batches of soup have somewhere to simmer.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Port for the smaller batch? I will keep the bottle away from the hob.

narrative.scene: A bottle of sweet wine stands where you expected cookware. The shopkeeper pulls out the cooking catalogue.
narrative.prompt: We seem to have taken a turn through the wine section. Ask again for your soup equipment.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A cooking pot! The bottle goes back on its shelf and your soup plan is back on track.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: More port? The wine shelf is getting busy while the soup ingredients wait.

narrative.scene: Two cooking vessels are packed. The shopkeeper asks what item to put on the gift receipt for a third order.
narrative.prompt: Your cooking club wants one too. Make the same request for the club's kitchen.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pot for the cooking club is on the receipt. Soup night is ready to begin.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Port for the cooking club is on the receipt. Someone had better bring the cookware!

narrative.scene: Your first cooking vessel is packed, but the second order contains a bottle. The shopkeeper opens the returns form.
narrative.prompt: Let us correct the second order before you leave. Tell me what belongs with the soup ingredients.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pot replaces the bottle on the second order. Both cooking stations can get started.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Port stays on the second order. The shopkeeper adds a reminder to borrow some cookware.

narrative.scene: The wine bottle is back on the shelf. Your new cooking vessel is packed and the shopkeeper starts a demonstration.
narrative.prompt: We need another vessel for the demonstration hob. Ask me for it.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pot goes on the demonstration hob. The vegetables are ready for their close-up.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Port arrives at the demonstration hob. The shopkeeper wisely leaves the bottle unopened.

narrative.scene: Two bottles are waiting at the till. The shopkeeper leads you to a shelf labelled Cookware.
narrative.prompt: We have reached the right shelf. Ask once more for the thing you need to cook your soup.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pot comes off the cookware shelf. Your soup finally has a home.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Port sends us back to the wine shelf. This shopping trip may need a separate cookware list!

target.title: The Prickly Autograph
target.premise: You are signing a poster at an art fair, but you have nothing to write with.
target.phrase_ipa: p l iː z p ɑː s m iː ə p e n

narrative.scene: Your first fan has an autograph. Another fan arrives with a glossy poster and no writing tool.
narrative.prompt: This poster needs a signature too. Ask me for the writing tool again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Here is a fresh pen. The second poster gets a bright blue signature.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Here is a pin. The second poster can go on the wall, but the autograph will have to wait.

narrative.scene: The poster is neatly fastened to a board, but your fan is still waiting for a signature.
narrative.prompt: We have solved the hanging problem. Tell me what you need to write the autograph.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen! The poster gets its signature and the fan gives a happy wave.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pin again? The poster is very securely displayed, but still unsigned.

narrative.scene: Two signed posters are drying. The assistant brings a guest book for the exhibition entrance.
narrative.prompt: The guest book needs your signature as well. Ask for the writing tool one last time.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen glides across the guest book. Your first signing session is complete.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pin lands beside the guest book. We can hang the book up, but we cannot sign with that!

narrative.scene: The first poster is signed. The second has been pinned to a board without an autograph.
narrative.prompt: Your second fan is waiting patiently. Ask me for the tool that will finish the signature.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen finishes the second signature. Both fans leave with the autograph they wanted.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Another pin holds the second poster even more firmly. The fan asks whether the signature is invisible.

narrative.scene: The displayed poster finally has its autograph. The assistant offers a card for the next fan.
narrative.prompt: One more fan would love a message. Ask for the writing tool for this card.
narrative.intended_dialogue: Here is a pen for the card. A small thank-you message makes the next fan smile.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: Here is a pin for the card. The next fan has received a very practical noticeboard accessory.

narrative.scene: The unsigned poster has acquired an impressive row of fasteners. The assistant opens the stationery drawer.
narrative.prompt: Let us focus on the signature now. Ask once more for what you need to write.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A pen at last! The poster gains its autograph beside its magnificent row of fasteners.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A pin at last? The assistant suggests opening a poster-hanging business after the signing session.

target.title: The Portrait First-aid Kit
target.premise: At a pet portrait studio, your kitten has curled up on your sleeve.
target.phrase: Look at the cat on my arm.
target.phrase_ipa: l ʊ k ə t ð ə k æ t ɒ n m aɪ ɑː m

narrative.scene: The artist has sketched the kitten's whiskers. Your little model turns to show its other side.
narrative.prompt: What should I look at for the next part of the portrait? Point it out again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: The cat has wonderful stripes on this side. I will add them to the sketch.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A cut on that side? I have put the pencils down and brought the first-aid box.

narrative.scene: The artist returns with a first-aid box. Your kitten is still curled up peacefully on your sleeve.
narrative.prompt: You seem comfortable, so perhaps I misunderstood. Tell me what to look at again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: A cat! I can put the bandages away and draw your very patient little model.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A cut again? I will keep the first-aid box nearby while you explain.

narrative.scene: Whiskers and stripes are on the page. The kitten lifts one paw while the artist reaches for a coloured pencil.
narrative.prompt: I need one last look before I colour the portrait. Direct my attention again.
narrative.intended_dialogue: The cat holds its paw still just long enough. Your pet portrait is finished!
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A cut needs attention before colouring. The portrait can wait while we check that you are comfortable.

narrative.scene: The whiskers are drawn, but the artist has paused the portrait to check the supposed injury.
narrative.prompt: If I have misunderstood, point out the subject of the portrait once more.
narrative.intended_dialogue: The cat is the subject, of course! The first-aid box closes and the portrait resumes.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: The cut is still your concern. I will leave the portrait safely on the easel while you get help if needed.

narrative.scene: The first-aid box is closed and the artist has begun drawing. The kitten settles into a new pose.
narrative.prompt: Our little model has moved. Show me where to look for the final sketch.
narrative.intended_dialogue: The cat is tucked against your sleeve. One soft pencil stroke finishes the portrait.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: A cut on your arm? I will pause again so you can check whether you need any help.

narrative.scene: The portrait is paused and the artist keeps the first-aid box on the table. The kitten gives a soft purr.
narrative.prompt: Before we decide what to do next, tell me once more what you want me to notice.
narrative.intended_dialogue: The cat was there all along! Its purr becomes the happy ending to our portrait session.
narrative.alternate_dialogue: The cut is what you want me to notice. We will keep the portrait for later and make sure you can get help.
